jobs.title: Principal, Product Owner (Copilot Studio)
jobs.description:
About Invesco

As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco.

What’s in it for you?

Our people are at the very core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including:
Flexible paid time off
Hybrid work schedule
401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution
Health & wellbeing benefits
Parental Leave benefits
Employee stock purchase plan

Job Description

Invesco is expanding its Microsoft Copilot Studio platform to support agent based AI capabilities across the Asset Management value chain. As part of this expansion, we are establishing Technical Product Owners (TPOs) who will own AI agents and capabilities from concept through production and scale.

This role is accountable for ensuring Copilot Studio agents deliver measurable business value, are built to enterprise standards, and scale responsibly across a large developer community.

You will be Responsibilities For:

Serve as the single accountable owner for a portfolio of Copilot Studio agents, capabilities, or agent families aligned to Invesco domains (e.g., Investments, Research, Product Information, Client Reporting, Operations, Risk & Compliance).
Define and communicate clear product vision, scope, and success metrics.
Own the full lifecycle of agents from ideation and MVP through production deployment and ongoing enhancement.
Act as a trusted partner to business stakeholders across Investments, Distribution, Operations, Risk, Compliance, and Technology Domain Owners.
Translate asset management workflows and pain points into well‑defined user stories, agent behaviors, and functional requirements.
Balance business ambition with practical constraints related to data, risk, and platform maturity.
Own the functional and technical definition of Copilot Studio agents in partnership with developers and platform teams.
Define agent instructions, guardrails, tone, and response constraints appropriate for financial services use.
Guide decisions on data sourcing, integrations, APIs, and reuse of components to ensure scalability, reusability, testing, and maintainability.
Demonstrate a solid understanding of large language model (LLM) fundamentals, including system prompts, few-shot prompting, and chain-of-thought reasoning, to effectively collaborate with business partners in designing agent behaviors.
Apply knowledge of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques to ensure agents access proprietary investment data (e.g., PDFs, research reports) accurately, minimizing hallucinations and providing grounded responses.
Evaluate trade-offs between model performance (e.g., GPT-4o vs. lighter models) and operational factors such as cost and response speed to optimize agent efficiency.
Leverage familiarity with Microsoft Power Platform, Power Automate, and Custom Connectors to define requirements for seamless data integration from internal databases and third-party providers (e.g., Bloomberg, Morningstar).
Ensure secure and compliant data access by understanding OAuth, service principals, JSON payload structuring, and implementing safety guardrails to prevent data leakage or unauthorized financial advice.
Ensure all owned agents comply with enterprise security, data protection, and regulatory requirements.
Serve as the product representative in architecture, security, and governance reviews.
Document intended use, limitations, assumptions, and known risks for each agent.
Act as the primary product point of contact for Copilot Studio developers working on owned capabilities.
Provide clear acceptance criteria, quality standards, and product guardrails.
Reduce duplication and “use‑case sprawl” by promoting shared capabilities and repeatable patterns.
Partner with platform teams to improve developer experience and accelerate responsible adoption at scale.
Define and monitor success metrics such as adoption, usage, time savings, quality improvement, and risk reduction.
Assess agent performance and user feedback to guide prioritization and enhancements.

The Experience You Brings

5 to 10 years of measurable experience in product ownership and industry.
Strong understanding of the Asset Management business, including investments, products, client servicing, or operations.
Ability to engage credibly with business leaders and subject matter experts.
Experience translating complex business workflows into actionable product requirements.
Familiarity with Microsoft Copilot Studio, Power Platform concepts, or similar AI / low‑code platforms.
Understanding of prompt and instruction design, data integration patterns, and AI limitations.
Comfort working closely with engineers, architects, data teams, and security partners.
Proven experience in product ownership, product management, or business‑focused technology roles.
Strong prioritization, backlog management, and decision‑making skills.
Experience operating in governed or regulated environments preferred.

The salary range for this position in Atlanta, GA is $140,000 - $155,000 year. The total compensation offered for this position includes salary and incentive pay and will vary based on skills, experience and location

Full Time / Part Time

Full time

Worker Type

Employee

Job Exempt (Yes / No)

Yes

Workplace Model

Pursuant to Invesco’s Workplace Policy, employees are expected to comply with the firm’s most current workplace model, which as of October 1, 2025, includes spending at least four full days each week working in an Invesco office. This reflects our belief that spending time together in the office helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more easily, and support each other’s growth and development.

The above information on this description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this role. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. The job holder may be required to perform other duties as deemed appropriate by their manager from time to time.

Invesco's culture of inclusivity and its commitment to diversity in the workplace are demonstrated through our people practices. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, citizenship status, disability, age, or veteran status. Our equal opportunity employment efforts comply with all applicable U.S. state and federal laws governing non-discrimination in employment.

jobs.title: Vice President, Product
jobs.description:
CANDIDATES MUST BE LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES**

About SafelyYou

SafelyYou’s passionate mission is to empower safer, more person-centered care across senior living through world-leading AI, industry-changing hardware, and remote expert clinicians, significantly improving outcomes for residents while increasing peace of mind for families and reducing costs for communities.

Originating in 2015 as the doctoral research of CEO George Netscher—and inspired by his own family's experience with Alzheimer's disease—SafelyYou was spun out of UC Berkeley’s Artificial Intelligence Research Lab, one of the top five AI research groups in the world. And today, our company is solving critical challenges in senior living, from resident falls and ER visits to staffing concerns, length of stay, and NOI. All helping ensure that communities can focus on improved care for residents while still reaching their financial goals.

SafelyYou is one of five most innovative fall technologies referenced in the Senate Falls Report (2019), a winner of the McKnight’s Tech Partner of the Year, and has been named to Fortune’s Impact 20 list, which recognizes companies making people’s lives better through innovation.

Your Role at SafelyYou

Our product works; how we build hasn't kept up. Our product and technology teams own customer outcomes, built on shared platforms. As VP of Product, you lead the product management team and own the portfolio: one committed roadmap, where investment goes, and which bets get funded, changed, or stopped. The CPTO sets overall direction and the VP of Engineering owns delivery; you own product execution You'll inherit a capable team ready for a stronger operating model, and part of the job is deciding what to keep, rebuild, and stop. Operators are choosing their technology partners for the next decade, and you'll have a seat at the leadership table as we earn that choice. Every improvement you ship reaches residents, families, and caregivers. You'll work daily with the CPTO and VP of Engineering, and closely with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, our clinical team, Operations, and Strategy.

Key Responsibilities

The Numbers You'll Own

Customer NOI. Own SafelyYou's impact on operator NOI per resident, proven with outcome data in each care setting.
Wellness AI and staffing intelligence. Build both into scaled product lines alongside Safety AI.
Throughput. Double the rate of committed features launched to customers within the next year, measured by release to market and adoption, not tickets closed.

What You'll Own

One roadmap. A single customer-facing roadmap tied to company objectives. Sales sells what's committed.
The portfolio. Allocate investment across customer-facing teams, shared platforms (AI, data and integrations, devices, hardware), and longer-horizon bets, and make stage-gate calls on evidence.
The operating model. With the VP of Engineering, run annual strategy, quarterly planning, and published decision rights. Build the operations support PMs need to focus on outcomes.
The ecosystem. Drive partner adoption so SafelyYou insights reach caregivers inside the EHR and eCall systems they already use.
Trusted AI. Clear accuracy and false-alarm standards, privacy by design, and evidence before anything reaches the field.
The market. Be in the room with our largest operators, shape pricing and packaging with Sales and Marketing, and represent product at industry events and with investors.
The team. Coach, level, and hire product managers, and build a bench of future leaders.

The Ideal Candidate

The hard requirement: you've led product managers through an operating-model change, such as functional teams to outcome and platform teams, on products that combine hardware, AI/ML, and cloud software.
10+ years in product, including 5+ years leading PMs across multiple product areas.
AI/ML, hardware, and platform or partner-ecosystem products shipped to market, including stage-gated development, certification, and field reliability.
Enterprise B2B credibility. You've carried a product number, not just supported one.
A decisive player-coach and clear writer who earns engineering's respect.
Strongly preferred, and learnable: healthcare or senior living experience, and regulated products (HIPAA, life-safety).

Salary Range:
$260,000 - $280,000 USD commensurate with experience

Why Join Us? You Can Make a Difference!

SafelyYou offers a competitive compensation package, including but not limited to:

A mission-driven company culture
Fully remote
Competitive salary & benefits, including fully paid employee premiums for Medical, Dental, and Vision
401k Program
Monthly Education, Well-being & WFH stipends
Non-accrual PTO
Growth Potential
Company Retreats
Medical & Family/Parental Leave

At SafelyYou, we believe that a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace makes us a more relevant, competitive, and resilient company. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workforce that celebrates diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or family status, disability, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

We value all the perspectives our team members bring to the table, and that is why we don’t look for culture fit, but culture add. We want to hear from YOU! We encourage you to apply even if you do not fit 100% of the technical requirements.

SafelyYou is working to ensure the highest-quality care for seniors in any care setting, anywhere in the world, driven by proven AI, unmatched clinical expertise, and an immeasurable passion for caregiving.

jobs.title: Director of Product Design
jobs.description:
Job Description :

Design Director, Product Design and Prototyping

The job in one line

You lead the design of products. You define what they should be, you build working prototypes of them yourself, and you shape how they go to market.

Why this role exists

Most agencies answer a product question with a deck. We want to answer it with something running on a phone.
We are a creative team inside a company that builds and runs technology for some of the largest companies in the world. That is an unusual place to sit. It means the products we imagine are products we are actually positioned to build. What we have been missing is the person in the middle: someone who can hold the product idea, the interface, and the market story at the same time, and who can make a real version of it in days instead of quarters.

That person did not exist five years ago at a price anyone could afford. Building a convincing prototype used to require an engineer. It does not anymore. AI tools have moved the hard part from writing the code to knowing what to build and having the taste to judge it when it appears. That is a creative job, and it sits on our team.

What you will do

Define the product. Decide what the thing is. Which features, in what order, for which customer, solving which problem. You will write the kind of clear product definition a client can act on and an engineering team can build from — user stories, feature prioritization and acceptance criteria for the MVP, a roadmap past it, the go-to-market plan, and the foundation for how success gets measured once it is live. You will do this on client work, on pitches, and on products we invent ourselves.

Prototype it. Not slides of a product. The product. You will build interactive, clickable, working prototypes using AI tools such as Claude Code, Claude Design, Cursor, v0, Figma Make, and whatever replaces them next year. Fast and rough on Monday, convincing enough to put in front of a client CEO by Friday. Your prototypes are how the rest of us find out whether the idea is any good.

Land it. Design the go-to-market alongside the product itself. How it launches, who it is for, what it promises, how it gets adopted, how it earns its second version. On this team, the product and the story it tells are the same piece of work.

Lead the work through. You will direct the designers on the products you define — setting the bar, running the critique, making the calls when the work needs to get better. The prototype is yours alone. Everything after it is a team, and you lead it.

What this looks like in practice

A retail client asks us to reimagine their app. In week one you and a strategist map where the current app fails its customer. By week two you have written a feature definition and built three working prototypes of the ideas that matter most, so the pitch team is arguing about a real interaction instead of a wireframe. By week three you have the launch narrative. When we win, you stay on it and lead the design of the thing you defined. Then you do it again for a transportation client's AI travel companion, again for a product we are building for the C-suite, and again for the next one.

How we will know it is working

The prototypes are the visible part. The measurable part is what they do to everything downstream. Engineering teams ramp onto new client work faster, because the product is defined and demonstrable before they arrive. Analytics, QA and user testing set up faster, for the same reason. New business gets a working prototype in front of a client sooner and more often. Proactive ideation goes up in volume, because ideas can be shown instead of described. And we lean less on off-the-shelf capability, because building the right thing stops being expensive.

Who this is for

We are looking for one person who can hold three things at once. People arrive at that from different directions, and we are open about which.

You may come from product.

You have been a product manager or product leader who was never satisfied handing off a requirements document. You have shipped real products people use. You have opinions about interfaces. Somewhere in the last two years you started building your own prototypes with AI tools instead of waiting for a sprint, and you have not stopped.

You may come from creative technology or design engineering.

You have been the person in the agency who makes the thing that wins the pitch. You can code, or you can direct AI tools to code, well enough that your prototypes feel real. What you want next is ownership of the product itself, not just the demo of it. You are applying to be the person who decides what gets made and makes the first version of it.

What we will ask you to show us

We do not need an advertising reel. Bring us products you defined and shipped, and be ready to explain what you decided and why, including the decisions you got wrong. Bring us prototypes you built with your own hands, and walk us through the tools and the process. If you have a launch you shaped, bring the thinking behind it: who it was for, what it promised, how it landed. Three or four things, told well, beats a portfolio site.

What you will need

Ten or more years of work, with real seniority in product, product design, or creative technology. Demonstrated ownership of products that shipped, not just features that were specified. Fluency with AI-assisted building. This is not a bonus line at the bottom of the posting. It is most of the job. You should already be using these tools daily and have views about which ones are worth anything.

Enough technical understanding to talk credibly with engineers, scope what is feasible, and know when a prototype is lying about how hard something will be. Design judgment. You do not have to be the person who makes it beautiful, and you will work alongside people who are. But you have to know beautiful from ordinary and be able to say why. The ability to stand in front of a client's leadership and hold the room.

What this role is not

It is not a software engineering role. You will not own production code, you will not be on call, and you do not report into engineering. It is not a visual design role. There is design craft in this job, but it is in service of the product, and you will have designers around you. It is not a support function for other people's ideas. This is a seat where the ideas start. On the panel: yes, and for a different question than the last three. The other postings had one audience. This one has two — the candidate, and whoever approves the title and band. The document is written entirely for the first. Nothing in it is phrased in the vocabulary a job-architecture reviewer uses to size a role, which is the thing you actually need it to survive. So I'd seat it for that: a compensation or job-architecture analyst on whether this reads as a Design Director-band role, an executive recruiter who places hybrid product-creative people on whether the market recognizes what you're describing, and someone who's held this shape of job on whether the description matches the reality. Plus the random seat. That panel answers a question worth answering. A panel on tone would mostly tell you the writing is fine.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Field Systems (Salesforce)
jobs.description:
For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Smartsheet is looking for a Senior Product Manager to join the Field Systems team, the group responsible for designing, evolving, and scaling the commercial go-to market tools including CRM, e-signature, opportunity management, sales engagement, marketing automation, and forecasting platforms. You will own the product roadmap and serve as the connective tissue between business stakeholders and an agile delivery team to ensure the right work gets prioritized, scoped, and shipped at the right time.

This is a high-impact role at the intersection of enterprise systems, business strategy, and Scaled agile execution. You'll thrive here if you love translating complex business needs into clear, actionable requirements, leveraging modern AI tools to work smarter and faster, and partnering closely with sales, marketing, finance, and customer success to drive measurable outcomes.

You will report to our Director, Field Systems. This is a remote eligible position and you may work remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is registered.

You Will

Partner with the Director of Field Systems to define, maintain, and communicate a prioritized product roadmap aligned to company go-to-market objectives
Continuously assess the value, urgency, and feasibility of roadmap initiatives to ensure the team is always working on the highest-impact problems
Translate strategic priorities into quarterly PI (Program Increment) objectives within the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe)
Engage directly with internal stakeholders including Sales, Sales Operations, Marketing, Finance, Customer Success and Technical Support to deeply understand pain points, workflows, and business goals
Define clear epics, features, and user stories with well-articulated acceptance criteria.
Lead discovery activities including stakeholder interviews, process walkthroughs, and data analysis to inform solution design
Leverage AI tools such as Claude and Gemini to accelerate requirements documentation, synthesize stakeholder feedback, draft communications, and surface insights from data bringing a modern, AI-augmented approach to everyday PM work
Serve as the Product Owner for the agile team, owning and grooming the team backlog to ensure a healthy queue of well-refined work
Actively participate in SAFe ceremonies including PI Planning, Refinement, Sprint Planning, Sprint Retrospectives, and System Demos
Make real-time prioritization and trade-off decisions to keep the team moving and unblocked
Maintain transparent, proactive communication with stakeholders on roadmap status, delivery timelines, and change impacts
Build trust with business partners by consistently delivering on commitments and surfacing risks early
Collaborate with change management and enablement teams to ensure successful adoption of new capabilities
Define success metrics for features and initiatives; track outcomes post-deployment and use data to inform future prioritization
Drive retrospective insights from delivery into roadmap refinement and team process improvements

You Have

5+ years of product management experience, with at least 3 years focused on go-to market tools and platform products in an enterprise environment
Demonstrated experience working within SAFe or agile framework, including PI Planning and cross-team coordination
Strong product sense with experience balancing user needs, business value, and technical feasibility
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present confidently to senior leaders and technical teams alike
Experience writing detailed epics and features, lean business cases, and user stories with strong assumptions and acceptance criteria
Comfort with data including the ability to query data, interpret metrics, and build business cases
Salesforce Administrator or Business Analyst certification
Experience supporting sales operations, revenue operations, or marketing operations functions
Familiarity with CPQ, Sales Cloud, or Service Cloud implementations
Hands-on experience with AI productivity tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT) applied to PM workflows such as documentation, research, or analysis.
SAFe Product Owner/Product Manager certification
Legally eligible to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis

Current US Perks & Benefits

Employer subsidized medical/vision and dental coverage for full-time employees
401k Match to help you save for your future (50% of your contribution up to the first 6% of your eligible pay)
Monthly stipend to support your work and productivity
Flexible Time Away Program, plus Sick Time Off
US employees are automatically covered under Smartsheet-sponsored life insurance, short-term, and long-term disability plans
US employees receive 12 paid holidays per year
Up to 24 weeks of Parental Leave
Personal paid Volunteer Day to support our community
Opportunities for professional growth and development including access to Udemy online courses
Company Funded Perks, including a counseling membership, local retail discounts, and your own personal Smartsheet account
Teleworking options from any registered location in the U.S. (role specific)

Smartsheet provides a competitive base salary range for roles that may be hired in different geographic areas we are licensed to operate our business from. Actual compensation is determined by several factors including, but not limited to, level of professional, educational experience, skills, and specific candidate location. In addition, this role will be eligible for a market competitive incentive opportunity.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Agentic Commerce
jobs.description:
Job Description

Amex Digital Labs’ mission is to build the future of payments and membership, creating new value that evolves with our customers' needs and drives deeper engagement and loyalty. We leverage emerging technologies to deliver innovations that enhance how customers pay, travel, dine, and experience the brand.

We are seeking a Senior Product Manager to lead product strategy and platform development for Agentic Commerce at American Express. This position will focus on the strategy and execution required to enable seamless, secure agent-driven transactions, including defining the experiences, platform capabilities, and trust frameworks needed to scale across partners and future use cases. This person will build a strong command of emerging agentic commerce protocols, existing card payments infrastructure, and new interaction models. Partnering closely with engineering, product, and cross-functional teams, this Product Manager will shape intuitive and delightful commerce journeys powered by AI agents.

As a trusted, closed-loop network, American Express is uniquely positioned to extend its authentication, authorization, identity, and risk capabilities into AI-powered commerce experiences while preserving Card Member visibility and control over agent-initiated activity. By leveraging our membership model, premium brand, and differentiated data assets, this person will help define the experiences and capabilities that create value for Card Members, merchants, partners, and the broader ecosystem.

Responsibilities

Product Strategy and Roadmap

Partner across American Express to define and deliver foundational capabilities that enable secure, scalable agentic commerce across the payments ecosystem
Align product strategy, requirements, and roadmaps across issuer and network perspectives to ensure scalable and interoperable solutions
Keep a pulse on industry trends, balancing near-term execution priorities with long-term strategy to support the overall product vision

Platform Technology

Collaborate on the development of capabilities related to authentication, authorization, tokenization, spend controls, identity, merchant enablement, and trust infrastructure.
Drive alignment on long-term platform architecture, operating models, and ecosystem strategy to support future scale.
Partner deeply with engineering teams to understand and develop a perspective on how to apply evolving technologies (Agent-to-Agent Protocol, Agentic Payments Protocol, x402, Web Bot Auth, Trusted Agent Protocol, Model Context Protocol, and others) for AI agent-facilitated payments

Product Delivery & Partner Enablement

Balance the needs of customers, internal stakeholders, leadership, and external partners while working with engineering to identify technical solutions, shape product requirements, and deliver platform capabilities that advance Agentic Commerce experiences
Bring structure to ambiguous, cross-ecosystem problems by defining how data flows across merchants, PSPs, and AI/LLM partners to support fraud, servicing, and Card Member experiences
Work with Business Development teams to evaluate, influence and operationalize partner requirements, and with Product Enablement teams on go-to-market strategies

Risk and Compliance

Partner closely with Fraud and Servicing to define strategies for fraud prevention, dispute management, and call or chat handling related to agentic transactions
Partner with internal stakeholders such as Legal, Compliance, and Risk teams to develop and adhere to governance principles and payments regulations to ensure compliant and secure payment experiences

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

4+ years of experience in product management/development, or similar role
Enthusiasm for exceptional products and services, deep customer empathy, keen product intuition, and skilled at articulation of product functionality
Curiosity and a hunger to understand how things work, with the ability to use that knowledge to make connections, identify opportunities, and push the innovation agenda within a large company.
Highly organized self-starter with strong ownership mentality and business track record
Understanding of tech and product development processes, with the ability to communicate with and influence both technical and non-technical partners
Ability to reconcile competing needs across customers, stakeholders, and partners, making effective decisions and gaining buy in
Proven partner to engineering and comfortable discussing technical trade-offs; known as a business person who can talk tech
Detail oriented, able to identify key questions, and assess how pieces of the puzzle interact and affect the overall product
Ability to recognize issues quickly and determine how to get a resolution through creative and efficient problem solving
Skilled at balancing big picture strategy and tactical details
Team player, comfortable with ambiguity, adaptable, accountable, and highly organized
Excellent communication skills across cross functional teams with the ability to engage, influence, and inspire partners to drive collaboration and alignment.
Willingness to be creative within the bounds of the highly regulated financial services environment

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with digital payments including digital wallets, fraud prevention, disputes, and payment processing

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.

About Us

At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. From delivering differentiated products to providing world-class customer service, we operate with a strong risk mindset, ensuring we continue to uphold our brand promise of trust, security, and service.

As part of Team Amex, you’ll experience our powerful backing with comprehensive support for your holistic well-being and many opportunities to learn new skills, develop as a leader, and grow your career. Here, your voice and ideas matter, your work makes an impact, and together, you will help us define the future of American Express.

About The Team

We back you with benefits that support your holistic well-being so you can be and deliver your best. This means caring for you and your loved ones' physical, financial, and mental health, as well as providing the flexibility you need to thrive personally and professionally:

Competitive base salaries
Bonus incentives
6% Company Match on retirement savings plan
Free financial coaching and financial well-being support
Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and disability benefits
Flexible working model with hybrid, onsite or virtual arrangements depending on role and business need
20+ weeks paid parental leave for all parents, regardless of gender, offered for pregnancy, adoption or surrogacy
Free access to global on-site wellness centers staffed with nurses and doctors (depending on location)
Free and confidential counseling support through our Healthy Minds program
Career development and training opportunities

For a full list of Team Amex benefits, visit our Colleague Benefits Site .

new_jobs.title: Director of Product Design
new_jobs.description:
Job Description :

Design Director, Product Design and Prototyping

The job in one line

You lead the design of products. You define what they should be, you build working prototypes of them yourself, and you shape how they go to market.

Why this role exists

Most agencies answer a product question with a deck. We want to answer it with something running on a phone.
We are a creative team inside a company that builds and runs technology for some of the largest companies in the world. That is an unusual place to sit. It means the products we imagine are products we are actually positioned to build. What we have been missing is the person in the middle: someone who can hold the product idea, the interface, and the market story at the same time, and who can make a real version of it in days instead of quarters.

That person did not exist five years ago at a price anyone could afford. Building a convincing prototype used to require an engineer. It does not anymore. AI tools have moved the hard part from writing the code to knowing what to build and having the taste to judge it when it appears. That is a creative job, and it sits on our team.

What you will do

Define the product. Decide what the thing is. Which features, in what order, for which customer, solving which problem. You will write the kind of clear product definition a client can act on and an engineering team can build from — user stories, feature prioritization and acceptance criteria for the MVP, a roadmap past it, the go-to-market plan, and the foundation for how success gets measured once it is live. You will do this on client work, on pitches, and on products we invent ourselves.

Prototype it. Not slides of a product. The product. You will build interactive, clickable, working prototypes using AI tools such as Claude Code, Claude Design, Cursor, v0, Figma Make, and whatever replaces them next year. Fast and rough on Monday, convincing enough to put in front of a client CEO by Friday. Your prototypes are how the rest of us find out whether the idea is any good.

Land it. Design the go-to-market alongside the product itself. How it launches, who it is for, what it promises, how it gets adopted, how it earns its second version. On this team, the product and the story it tells are the same piece of work.

Lead the work through. You will direct the designers on the products you define — setting the bar, running the critique, making the calls when the work needs to get better. The prototype is yours alone. Everything after it is a team, and you lead it.

What this looks like in practice

A retail client asks us to reimagine their app. In week one you and a strategist map where the current app fails its customer. By week two you have written a feature definition and built three working prototypes of the ideas that matter most, so the pitch team is arguing about a real interaction instead of a wireframe. By week three you have the launch narrative. When we win, you stay on it and lead the design of the thing you defined. Then you do it again for a transportation client's AI travel companion, again for a product we are building for the C-suite, and again for the next one.

How we will know it is working

The prototypes are the visible part. The measurable part is what they do to everything downstream. Engineering teams ramp onto new client work faster, because the product is defined and demonstrable before they arrive. Analytics, QA and user testing set up faster, for the same reason. New business gets a working prototype in front of a client sooner and more often. Proactive ideation goes up in volume, because ideas can be shown instead of described. And we lean less on off-the-shelf capability, because building the right thing stops being expensive.

Who this is for

We are looking for one person who can hold three things at once. People arrive at that from different directions, and we are open about which.

You may come from product.

You have been a product manager or product leader who was never satisfied handing off a requirements document. You have shipped real products people use. You have opinions about interfaces. Somewhere in the last two years you started building your own prototypes with AI tools instead of waiting for a sprint, and you have not stopped.

You may come from creative technology or design engineering.

You have been the person in the agency who makes the thing that wins the pitch. You can code, or you can direct AI tools to code, well enough that your prototypes feel real. What you want next is ownership of the product itself, not just the demo of it. You are applying to be the person who decides what gets made and makes the first version of it.

What we will ask you to show us

We do not need an advertising reel. Bring us products you defined and shipped, and be ready to explain what you decided and why, including the decisions you got wrong. Bring us prototypes you built with your own hands, and walk us through the tools and the process. If you have a launch you shaped, bring the thinking behind it: who it was for, what it promised, how it landed. Three or four things, told well, beats a portfolio site.

What you will need

Ten or more years of work, with real seniority in product, product design, or creative technology. Demonstrated ownership of products that shipped, not just features that were specified. Fluency with AI-assisted building. This is not a bonus line at the bottom of the posting. It is most of the job. You should already be using these tools daily and have views about which ones are worth anything.

Enough technical understanding to talk credibly with engineers, scope what is feasible, and know when a prototype is lying about how hard something will be. Design judgment. You do not have to be the person who makes it beautiful, and you will work alongside people who are. But you have to know beautiful from ordinary and be able to say why. The ability to stand in front of a client's leadership and hold the room.

What this role is not

It is not a software engineering role. You will not own production code, you will not be on call, and you do not report into engineering. It is not a visual design role. There is design craft in this job, but it is in service of the product, and you will have designers around you. It is not a support function for other people's ideas. This is a seat where the ideas start. On the panel: yes, and for a different question than the last three. The other postings had one audience. This one has two — the candidate, and whoever approves the title and band. The document is written entirely for the first. Nothing in it is phrased in the vocabulary a job-architecture reviewer uses to size a role, which is the thing you actually need it to survive. So I'd seat it for that: a compensation or job-architecture analyst on whether this reads as a Design Director-band role, an executive recruiter who places hybrid product-creative people on whether the market recognizes what you're describing, and someone who's held this shape of job on whether the description matches the reality. Plus the random seat. That panel answers a question worth answering. A panel on tone would mostly tell you the writing is fine.
